question.:question/problem:
Use the transformation $y=v(x)x$ to find the general solution of the following homogeneous differential equation.

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{x^2+3y^2}{2xy}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
With $y=v(x)x$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}&=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(x) \\ &=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{1x^2+3(vx)^2}{2x(vx)} \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{1+3v^2}{2v} \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{1+v^2}{2v} \\ \frac{2v}{1+v^2}\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{1}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\int\frac{2v}{1+v^2}\,\mathrm{d}v&=\int\frac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ \ln(1+v^2)&=\ln|x|+C_1 \\ 1+v^2&=Kx \\ v^2&=Kx-1\end{aligned}
$$

From the transformation $y=vx$, we get

$$
v=\frac{y}{x}.
$$

Substituting the above into our solution, we finally obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{y^2}{x^2}&=Kx-1 \\ y^2&=Kx^3-x^2\end{aligned}
$$

Here $K$ absorbs the exponential constant and the sign of $x$ on the interval. Use real branches where the original equation is defined.

The solution is used on intervals where $x\ne0$ and $y\ne0$.

question.:question/problem:
Find the general solution of the following differential equation.

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{y^2-x^2}{xy}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
This is a homogeneous equation because all terms in the numerator and denominator have degree 2 (quadratic).

With $y=v(x)x$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}&=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(x) \\ &=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{(vx)^2-x^2}{x(vx)} \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{v^2-1}{v} \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{v^2-1}{v}-v=-\frac{1}{v} \\ v\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=-\frac{1}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\int v\,\mathrm{d}v&=-\int\frac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ \frac{v^2}{2}&=-\ln|x|+C_1 \\ v^2&=-2\ln|x|+C\end{aligned}
$$

From the transformation $y=vx$, we get

$$
v=\frac{y}{x}.
$$

Substituting the above into our solution, we finally obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{y^2}{x^2}&=-2\ln|x|+C \\ \frac{y^2}{x^2}&=-\ln(x^2)+C \\ y^2&=-x^2\ln(x^2)+Cx^2\end{aligned}
$$

Here $C=2C_1$; use $2\ln|x|=\ln(x^2)$.

The solution is used on intervals where $x\ne0$ and $y\ne0$.

question.:question/problem:
Use the transformation $y=v(x)x$ to find the general solution of the following homogeneous differential equation. Consider the solutions with $y\ne0$.

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{yx}{y^2+x^2}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
With $y=v(x)x$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}&=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(x) \\ &=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{(vx)x}{(vx)^2+x^2} \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{v}{v^2+1} \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{v}{v^2+1}-v=-\frac{v^3}{v^2+1} \\ \frac{v^2+1}{v^3}\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=-\frac{1}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\int\frac{v^2+1}{v^3}\,\mathrm{d}v&=-\int\frac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ \int\left(\frac{1}{v}+\frac{1}{v^3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}v&=-\ln|x|+C_1 \\ \ln|v|-\frac{1}{2v^2}&=-\ln|x|+C_1 \\ 2\ln|v|-\frac{1}{v^2}&=-2\ln|x|+C\end{aligned}
$$

From the transformation $y=vx$, we get

$$
v=\frac{y}{x}.
$$

Substituting the above into our solution, we finally obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2\ln\left|\frac{y}{x}\right|-\frac{x^2}{y^2}&=-2\ln|x|+C \\ 2\ln\left|\frac{y}{x}\right|+2\ln|x|-\frac{x^2}{y^2}&=C \\ 2\ln|y|-\frac{x^2}{y^2}&=C\end{aligned}
$$

Here $C=2C_1$. The constant solution $y=0$ was excluded by the question; division by $v$ is therefore valid.

The solution is used on intervals where $x\ne0$ and $y\ne0$.

question.:question/problem:
Find the general solution of the following differential equation.

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{y^3+xy^2+x^2y+x^3}{xy^2+x^2y}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
This is a homogeneous equation because all terms in the numerator and denominator have degree 3 (cubic).

With $y=v(x)x$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}&=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(x) \\ &=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{(vx)^3+x(vx)^2+x^2(vx)+x^3}{x(vx)^2+x^2(vx)} \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{v^3+v^2+v+1}{v^2+v} \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{v^3+v^2+v+1}{v^2+v}-v \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{(v+1)}{v(v+1)}=\frac{1}{v} \\ v\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{1}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\int v\,\mathrm{d}v&=\int\frac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ \frac{v^2}{2}&=\ln|x|+C_1 \\ v^2&=2\ln|x|+C\end{aligned}
$$

From the transformation $y=vx$, we get

$$
v=\frac{y}{x}.
$$

Substituting the above into our solution, we finally obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{y^2}{x^2}&=2\ln|x|+C \\ y^2&=x^2(2\ln|x|+C)\end{aligned}
$$

Here $C=2C_1$. The original denominator excludes $v=0$ and $v=-1$, so the cancellation is valid only on those intervals.

The solution is used on intervals where $x\ne0$, $y\ne0$, and $y\ne-x$.

question.:question/problem:
Use the transformation $y=v(x)x$ to find the general solution of the following homogeneous differential equation.

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{y}{x}\left(\ln\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)+1\right)
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
With $y=v(x)x$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}&=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(x) \\ &=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{vx}{x}\left(\ln\left(\frac{vx}{x}\right)+1\right) \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=v(\ln v+1) \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=v\ln v \\ \frac{1}{v\ln v}\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{1}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\int\frac{1}{v\ln v}\,\mathrm{d}v&=\int\frac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ u&=\ln v,\qquad \frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}v}=\frac{1}{v} \\ \int\frac{1}{u}\,\mathrm{d}u&=\ln|x|+C \\ \ln|\ln v|&=\ln|x|+C\end{aligned}
$$

From the transformation $y=vx$, we get

$$
v=\frac{y}{x}.
$$

Substituting the above into our solution, we finally obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\ln\left|\ln\frac{y}{x}\right|&=\ln|x|+C \\ \left|\ln\frac{y}{x}\right|&=e^C|x|^{1} \\ \ln\frac{y}{x}&=Kx \\ \frac{y}{x}&=e^{Kx} \\ y&=xe^{Kx}\end{aligned}
$$

The signed constant $K$ absorbs $e^C$ and the fixed sign of $x$ on the interval. The division by $\ln v$ excluded $v=1$; restoring it allows $K=0$, giving $y=x$.

The solution is used on intervals where $x\ne0$ and $y/x>0$.

question.:question/problem:
Use the transformation $y=v(x)x$ to find the general solution of the following homogeneous differential equation. Consider the solutions with $y\ne0$.

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{y^3}{xy^2+x^3}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
With $y=v(x)x$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}&=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(x) \\ &=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{(vx)^3}{x(vx)^2+x^3} \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{v^3}{v^2+1} \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{v^3}{v^2+1}-v=-\frac{v}{v^2+1} \\ \frac{v^2+1}{v}\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=-\frac{1}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\int\frac{v^2+1}{v}\,\mathrm{d}v&=-\int\frac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ \int\left(v+\frac{1}{v}\right)\,\mathrm{d}v&=-\ln|x|+C_1 \\ \frac{v^2}{2}+\ln|v|&=-\ln|x|+C_1 \\ v^2+\ln(v^2)&=-\ln(x^2)+C\end{aligned}
$$

From the transformation $y=vx$, we get

$$
v=\frac{y}{x}.
$$

Substituting the above into our solution, we finally obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{y^2}{x^2}+\ln\left(\frac{y^2}{x^2}\right)&=-\ln(x^2)+C \\ \frac{y^2}{x^2}+\ln(y^2)-\ln(x^2)&=-\ln(x^2)+C \\ \frac{y^2}{x^2}+\ln(y^2)&=C \\ \frac{y^2}{x^2}&=C-\ln(y^2) \\ \frac{y^2}{C-\ln(y^2)}&=x^2\end{aligned}
$$

Here $C=2C_1$. The constant solution $y=0$ was excluded by the question. On the nonzero solution, the final denominator equals $y^2/x^2>0$.

The solution is used on intervals where $x\ne0$ and $y\ne0$.

question.:question/problem:
Use the transformation $y=v(x)x$ to find the general solution of the following homogeneous differential equation.

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{x^3+y^3}{xy^2}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
With $y=v(x)x$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}&=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(x) \\ &=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{x^3+(vx)^3}{x(vx)^2} \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{1+v^3}{v^2}=\frac{1}{v^2}+v \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{1}{v^2} \\ v^2\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{1}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\int v^2\,\mathrm{d}v&=\int\frac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ \frac{v^3}{3}&=\ln|x|+C_1 \\ v^3&=3\ln|x|+C\end{aligned}
$$

From the transformation $y=vx$, we get

$$
v=\frac{y}{x}.
$$

Substituting the above into our solution, we finally obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)^3&=3\ln|x|+C \\ y^3&=x^3(3\ln|x|+C) \\ y&=x\sqrt[3]{3\ln|x|+C}\end{aligned}
$$

Here $C=3C_1$ and the cube root is real. Restrict the solution to intervals where $y\ne0$.

The solution is used on intervals where $x\ne0$ and $y\ne0$.

question.:question/problem:
Use the transformation $y=v(x)x$ to find the general solution of the following homogeneous differential equation.

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{x+2y}{x}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
With $y=v(x)x$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}&=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(x) \\ &=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{x+2(vx)}{x} \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=1+2v \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=1+v \\ \frac{1}{1+v}\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{1}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\int\frac{1}{1+v}\,\mathrm{d}v&=\int\frac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ \ln|v+1|&=\ln|x|+C_1 \\ |v+1|&=e^{C_1}|x| \\ v+1&=Cx \\ v&=Cx-1\end{aligned}
$$

From the transformation $y=vx$, we get

$$
v=\frac{y}{x}.
$$

Substituting the above into our solution, we finally obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{y}{x}&=Cx-1 \\ y&=Cx^2-x\end{aligned}
$$

The signed constant $C$ absorbs $e^{C_1}$. Division by $v+1$ excluded $v=-1$; restoring it permits $C=0$, giving $y=-x$.

The solution is used on intervals where $x\ne0$.

question.:question/problem:
Use the transformation $y=v(x)x$ to find the general solution of the following homogeneous differential equation.

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{x+y}{x}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
With $y=v(x)x$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}&=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(x) \\ &=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{x+(vx)}{x} \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=1+v \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=1 \\ \frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{1}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\int\mathrm{d}v&=\int\frac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ v&=\ln|x|+C\end{aligned}
$$

From the transformation $y=vx$, we get

$$
v=\frac{y}{x}.
$$

Substituting the above into our solution, we finally obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{y}{x}&=\ln|x|+C \\ y&=x\ln|x|+Cx\end{aligned}
$$



The solution is used on intervals where $x\ne0$.
